title: F5: codex_reply works again — `codex exec resume` rejects -C; build the resume argv the CLI accepts and run it with cwd set to the worktree
spec:
Gotcha 2026-09-19 18:27: orchestrator/executor.py:51 builds every Codex command as ["codex", "exec", *args, "--json", "-C", cwd, *access]; for a fix round args = ["resume", thread, delta], and the installed Codex CLI answers: error: unexpected argument '-C' found. Usage: codex exec resume [OPTIONS] [SESSION_ID] [PROMPT]. So codex_reply (executor.reply) has failed on every fix round since Codex returned; the round counter still incremented (T-0242 rounds 1) and the task stayed running.
Change executor.py:
1. Run `codex exec resume --help` once (record the accepted options in the module docstring) and build the resume argv accordingly: the working directory goes to subprocess cwd (the worktree) instead of -C when resume does not accept -C; keep --json only if resume accepts it, otherwise parse the plain final message (last non-empty stdout paragraph) so out["message"] is still filled; keep the sandbox/access flags only where accepted. Fresh `codex exec` argv stays byte-identical.
2. Split the argv construction into a pure function argv_for(kind, ...) with kind in {"exec", "resume"} so tests can assert both shapes without spawning codex.
3. On a CLI usage error (rc 2 with 'unexpected argument' or 'Usage:' in stderr) return status failed with reason prefixed 'codex argv error:' and do not increment rounds.
Tests in tests/test_executor.py: test_resume_argv_has_no_C_flag_and_uses_cwd, test_exec_argv_unchanged, test_usage_error_does_not_count_round (subprocess.run monkeypatched). Final message: paste the `codex exec resume --help` option list you observed.
acceptance: final message lists the options `codex exec resume --help` printed on this machine and the argv shape chosen
Existing tests pass; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0 in the worktree

Tests test_resume_argv_has_no_C_flag_and_uses_cwd, test_exec_argv_unchanged, test_usage_error_does_not_count_round added. tests-green.sh wt/T-0249 exited 0 (Planner, 19:05).
